reviews.author: Carly Stice
reviews.text: Wow! I have never been to a fort that is so well maintained. Amazing time getting to walk through the facility. I will say if you have small children, keep a close eye on them there are some drop offs and the area is pretty unrestricted.

reviews.author: Michael Machado
reviews.text:
The Park seemed to be a pretty good size. We happened to go on a rainy, very windy day so we were not able to walk around to everything and earlu January there is not much going on and the lighthouse was closed.
Some of the bunkers are left open and you can easily walk through them. The bunkers look well maintained as well as the surrounding grounds.

reviews.author: Sofia’s Photos
reviews.text:
This place is very dear to my heart. Years ago, one of the most meaningful photo sessions of my career happened here, and it unexpectedly reached millions of people online.
What makes this spot so special is the atmosphere, the beautiful views, and the iconic lighthouse. Sometimes it’s open, and we were once lucky enough to go inside during a wedding photo session, which made the experience unforgettable.
I always love coming back here. Some places are simply beautiful. Others become part of your story.

reviews.author: Nancy Valleroy-Jenkins
reviews.text: Amazing place! Lots of history and information, safe, trails, well kept, gorgeous views! The fort itself is very interesting and well preserved. The lighthouse is full of more history and like access to the past.

reviews.author: Kevin Vickery
reviews.text:
Historic fort from a century ago, with battlements perched atop hills overlooking Puget Sound. Acres of grass to wander, between relics of the past.

Keep your eyes out for deer, rabbits, chipmunks and many different bird species.

Admiralty Head Lighthouse sits on the grounds as well.

reviews.author: Kent
reviews.text: Great location right in front of the sound. Found the sight of the ferry pulling in every so often fascinating and was a unique experience seeing it juxtaposed against RVs. The beach area is lovely with lots of driftwood and it was fun to be able to try salmon fishing from shore just 3 min walk from our RV and the fort has nice views and history. Middle sites are a bit cramped. The site host was very kind and checked up on us when we checked in late and in the dark missed our site few times. He even helped us back the trailer in (as we had some issues with the angle). Usage of Deception pass dump sight 20 min away was free. T-mobile reception wasn't good. Looking forward to coming back again!

reviews.author: John
reviews.text: We camped here during the Thanksgiving Holiday. We were surprised at how full it was for a cold Holiday weekend. Everyone was very respectful. The site we stayed at had no hookups. We enjoyed exploring the old fort and lighthouse. We enjoyed watching the ferries as well.

reviews.author: BurntFrog Life
reviews.text: Wide open campground, with not trees. Our campsite, #28 gets the first shade. Thanks to the Senior WA Winter Camping Pass, a site with electricity is only $10 per night. The campsite is only a 10 minute walk to the ferry terminal for visiting Port Townsend. The gun battery installations are fascinating and so well preserved. Lots of history here. We spent 3 days over in Port Townsend seeing the sites there. I was very happy with the campground and even though it is wide open, we didn't feel privacy was an issue as there aren't alot of campers this time of year. Joan, the camp host is the best!

I've been coming to Fort Casey for multiple decades, starting long before the campground was here. This campground was one of my folks favorite places when they retired. There's essentially no shade until an hour or so before sunset, depending on your site. In addition to the beach and the fort, ferry watching can be fun. One of the th... [正文在页面被截断]

reviews.author: Marky-Mark
reviews.text: Fort Casey is a beautiful campground right on the Sound with views that are incredible. Sites on the perimeter have nice spacing to them, and many have water and power. Watching the ferry come and go is fun, along with all of the hiking right next door. But unfortunately they have a camp host who is rude at best and never around. Tried to get hold of him 3 different times with no luck. Rumor has it that he spends his time up at the rangers office instead of assisting campers which is what that job asks of those who volunteer. Sure hope the parks department finds a new host as there were many who were complaining about him.

reviews.author: camp-dwightmatheny
reviews.text: We had a great stay at Fort Casey in dry camping site 25. Lots of privacy and pretty level. Waterfront site with view of ferry right in front of us. Callan's restaurant within walking distance had great food and delicious cookies! Don't miss exploring the batteries and lighthouse above. Would be a good place to walk on ferry and explore Port Townsend for the day. Only issue, as noted by others, was jet noise from flyovers until 11 pm!

This is SUCH a beautiful park! However...we will never come back here. We had our Airstream on a water no hook up site, beautiful views of the water, mountains, several bald eagles, orcas, seals, it is a beautiful spot! The fort is a fun place to explore and the views are expansive. Watching the ferries come and go is always such a fun treat. We will NOT come back here, ever. The Navy ran flight drills right over head every.single.day. we were there. It was so loud it shook the Airstream every time they flew over, and they fly very low because they practice "touch and goes" (where they fly, land and then fly right back up to practice for landing on aircraft carries). Most drills were around 6 or 7 hours a day. There was a day or two in there where they started at 9 in the morning and at 9PM they were still doing drills. The sound was so incredibly loud and they fly so incredibly close. The first day, we really enjoyed the experience and thought it was really cool! However, by day 5 we ended our 7 day trip early because we couldn't handle the noise anymore. It ruined being outside enjoying nature, the sound is awful. My heart goes out to all the lovely people who live on Whidbey or retired there for the gorgeous natural sanctuary, that is disturbed by these drills. My husband is a veteran and my family members are veterans, we support our military but the location of these drills seem like a terrible idea.

reviews.author: Wolbee
reviews.text: Stayed here on Memorial Day. Did not have the best spot but the views of Admiralty Inlet, Olympic and Cascade mountains with the back drop of old bunkers and a cool lighthouse is amazing. We saw Orca whales in inlet that swam right next to the bay near our campground that made this trip very special. There are only a few spots with hook ups but there is a water fill station near restroom/showers (which are really clean).. we were fortunate to have a goos solar system so was not a big deal. Camp host and staff of park were very nice.

reviews.author: camp-roadtripper431199
reviews.text: We were in site 7 directly across from the restrooms, which were IMMACULATELY clean!! Showers available for .50/3 minutes. Bunnies coming in and out of the brush along with deer grazing through your site. Easy walk to the beach and up the hill to Fort Casey State Park and Admiralty Head Lighthouse.

reviews.author: CarmenV3
reviews.text: This place is truly amazing. The setting is gorgeous; truly a PNW treasure. You have the mountains, ocean & forest to explore and enjoy. Spend the day learning history or finding some of the many wild animals in the park. If peace and solitude is what you want, take a walk in the forest, on the beach or take a nap on the grassy knoll under the trees. If you need some adrenaline- go fishing (seasonal), watch fighter jets from nearby base fly over you or listen for the ferry horn and watch it go in/pit of the dock. Most definitely plan to return again.

What a great little campground for those who are looking for a waterfront camping experience. The sites are decent size but have no privacy between them in case your wanting that. Restrooms were kept very clean, but here's the kicker unfortunately. The campground host is the most rude and condescending host I've ever come across. We arrived and although his sign said he was On Duty he was nowhere to be found so we headed to our reserved space. An hour or two later he shows up and demandingly states we have to register. Well I've been camping lots of times and have never even had a park ranger let alone a camp host get so agitated over such a small thing. My guess is he does this because he does not actually work and go around the campground to see who’s arrived, he waits to give you crap after. Then another camper tells me about how rude he was with them telling them he was going to have the ranger come and speak with them after they asked him why he was so angry with his approach after mistaking their spot with another one, and the other party not even being concerned about it at all. Last, I hear another camper tell me that she knows he goes and hangs out at the ranger station to avoid doing what’s asked of camp hosts and obviously to try and increase his authority over others. We tried numerous times, when his sign said ON DUTY to get wood and ice but to no avail. Interestingly his truck was parked there next to his trailer but he wouldn't answer the knocks on his door, I say this because he wasn't in the campground anywhere so he more than likely was inside unless paling around in the rangers truck. Gary needs to be removed from the role of being a campground host anywhere, that's not what people are expecting when they go to camp, especially at such a nice gem like Fort Casey.

Spent two wonderful days camped here with our fifth wheel. We were in site 14 which has a wonderful ocean side view. This site is not serviced, but there are sites in the campground that have power and water, however they did not have the ocean side view that we had. The site is large, but not very private, but with that view who cares. Large picnic table provide, the site is level, with a good gravel area to park the RV. Water is available at the washrooms, so you can fill your fresh water tank. There are a number of large trash containers around, so you can ensure no visits from crows or gulls. It can be a little windy, but after all, you are on the ocean, so you should expect it. Lots to see, and do, around the old military fort, with the gun mounts, installations etc. I would recommend this for anyone, that want to relax ocean side. We enjoyed the solitude, the views of all the ships traveling up the water way, Ocean cruise ships, naval vessels, commercial container ships, there was always something to get the binoculars out, and take a look. Nice site to spend a few days. (Note, no dump site for your black water, so plan accordingly)

reviews.author: Colleen T.
reviews.text: We love this small waterfront campground. Great beach and views with historic fort and bunkers. View if boats and cruise ships coming and going.

reviews.author: Rena L.
reviews.text: This campground was the first we visited on the way up the island from the ferry. It is tiny and right next to the ferry dock with no cover or shade from the sun. Seeing the ferry come and go is neat but gets tiring. The spaces are close together and there is literally no privacy. You can choose a better campground by going further up the island.
